key_insight: Bag-of-waves turns EEG into interpretable waveform tokens learned without labels, enabling competitive classification with far less data and far better transparency than deep models.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical low-data EEG pipeline that can support clinical decision systems where interpretability, parameter efficiency, and waveform auditability matter.
method: Learn a small shift-invariant dictionary of recurring EEG waveform atoms from unlabeled signals.
Convert continuous EEG into atom tokens and use their counts for classification or clustering.
Extend tokens with n-grams for temporal transitions and spatial atoms for multichannel regional patterns.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on three datasets spanning low-data mouse genotype clustering, dementia resting-state classification, and the six-class TUEV benchmark, with performance competitive with deep and foundation baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and stability of learned atoms, so dictionary size, shift-invariance settings, and channel montage choices need careful tuning to avoid missing rare or subtle events.
paper_title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
